subject: Social Habits
title: Toilet and clean hands
subtopics: Telling the teacher I need the toilet
objectives: Children will tell an adult when they need the toilet.
Children will wash their hands after using the toilet.
content: Telling the teacher when I need the toilet, washing my hands, and wiping and flushing with help.
teachingActivities: Treat accidents as normal and never shame a child; ask every child regularly and let them go when they need to; use simple words agreed with parents; model hand washing with a song; ensure a second adult is available; follow the school hygiene and safeguarding policy for toilet help.
learnerActivities: Tell an adult about toilet needs, use the toilet with support and wash hands with soap.
assessment: Observe whether each child tells an adult they need the toilet and washes hands with support.
expectedOutcomes: Tells an adult they need the toilet with a word or sign.

lessons.title: Telling the teacher
lessons.subject: Social Habits
lessons.subtopic: Telling the teacher I need the toilet
objectives: Children will tell an adult when they need the toilet with a word or sign.
successCriteria: Goes to the toilet with an adult
lessons.previousKnowledge: Children can follow routines, share and show kindness.
lessons.starter: Show the doll and say "Dolly needs the toilet. She tells her teacher: toilet please."
teacherActivities: Show how the doll tells the teacher "toilet please".
Say "We tell the teacher when we need the toilet."
Practise the word or sign with each child.
Take small groups to see the toilet room.
presentation: Step 1. Teacher: Show how the doll tells the teacher "toilet please". Children: Children watch and say toilet.
Step 2. Teacher: Say "We tell the teacher when we need the toilet." Children: Children repeat toilet please.
Step 3. Teacher: Practise the word or sign with each child. Children: Child says or signs toilet.
Step 4. Teacher: Take small groups to see the toilet room. Children: Children visit and look.

practical.title: Toilet words
practical.safety: Use only school-approved toilet routines with a second adult nearby and keep doors open or as the policy says. Never shame a child; accidents happen.

differentiation.support: Practise the word or sign with a doll first.
differentiation.extension: Ask the child to remind a friend to tell the teacher.

assessment.method: Observe each child during the practical activity and note Emerging, Developing, Secure or Exceeding on the class record. Ask the questions below one to one or in a small group.

expectedOutcomes: Visits the toilet room with an adult
lessons.conclusion: Sing the toilet song and wave.
lessons.homeConnection: Agree the same toilet word with your child at home and school.
teacherReflection: Which children could show "tell an adult when they need the toilet with a word or sign" without help, and who needs another turn tomorrow?
What did the children say or do that I did not expect, and how will I use it in the next lesson?
Which resource or instruction worked best, and what would I change before I teach this again?

lessons.title: Washing my hands
lessons.subject: Social Habits
objectives: Children will wash their hands with soap after using the toilet.
successCriteria: Washes hands with soap with support
lessons.previousKnowledge: Children can follow routines, share and show kindness.
lessons.starter: Show your hands and say "Hands must be clean. We wash with soap after the toilet."
teacherActivities: Show how to wet, soap, rub and rinse hands.
Sing the hand washing song while rubbing.
Show how to dry hands on a clean towel.
learnerActivities: Children watch and copy the actions.
presentation: Step 1. Teacher: Show how to wet, soap, rub and rinse hands. Children: Children watch and copy the actions.
Step 2. Teacher: Sing the hand washing song while rubbing. Children: Children sing and rub.
Step 3. Teacher: Show how to dry hands on a clean towel. Children: Child dries hands.
Step 4. Teacher: Say "Clean hands. Well done." Children: Children show their clean hands.

practical.title: Hand washing
practical.safety: Use mild soap and shallow water and wipe up spills. Supervise every child at the basin and use a clean towel for each child.

differentiation.support: Wash hands together with a hand over the child’s hand.
differentiation.extension: Ask the child to teach a friend to wash hands.

assessment.method: Observe each child during the practical activity and note Emerging, Developing, Secure or Exceeding on the class record. Ask the questions below one to one or in a small group.

expectedOutcomes: Washes hands with soap with support
lessons.homeConnection: Wash hands together after every toilet visit and before meals.
teacherReflection: Which children could show "wash their hands with soap after using the toilet" without help, and who needs another turn tomorrow?
What did the children say or do that I did not expect, and how will I use it in the next lesson?
Which resource or instruction worked best, and what would I change before I teach this again?

learnerFacing.songOrRhyme: Rub, rub, rub your hands, wash the dirt away.

lessons.title: Wiping and flushing
lessons.subject: Social Habits
objectives: Children will learn the steps after using the toilet with adult help.
successCriteria: Names the toilet steps in order
lessons.previousKnowledge: Children can follow routines, share and show kindness.
resources: Picture cards for the toilet steps
A doll and a toy toilet
lessons.starter: Show the picture cards and say "Toilet, wipe, flush, wash. Four steps to stay clean."
teacherActivities: Show each picture and say the step.
Use the doll and toy toilet to act out the steps.
learnerActivities: Children look and say the step.
Child places the cards in order.
presentation: Step 1. Teacher: Show each picture and say the step. Children: Children look and say the step.
Step 2. Teacher: Use the doll and toy toilet to act out the steps. Children: Children copy the actions.
Step 3. Teacher: Put the cards in order. Children: Child places the cards in order.
Step 4. Teacher: Say "I did it" when finished. Children: Children say I did it.

practical.title: Toilet steps
steps: Act the steps with the doll.
practical.safety: Use a doll and cards only and never ask a child to demonstrate on their own body. Keep to the school policy for toilet help.

differentiation.support: Point to each card and say the step together.
differentiation.extension: Ask the child to tell a friend the steps.

assessment.method: Observe each child during the practical activity and note Emerging, Developing, Secure or Exceeding on the class record. Ask the questions below one to one or in a small group.

questions.question: What do we do after the toilet?

lessons.conclusion: Sing the washing song and wave.
lessons.homeConnection: Talk through the toilet steps at home and praise each one.
teacherReflection: Which children could show "learn the steps after using the toilet with adult help" without help, and who needs another turn tomorrow?
What did the children say or do that I did not expect, and how will I use it in the next lesson?
Which resource or instruction worked best, and what would I change before I teach this again?

lessons.title: Clean hands every time
lessons.subject: Social Habits
objectives: Children will wash hands without being reminded after a toilet visit or before eating.
successCriteria: Goes to the basin when prompted
lessons.previousKnowledge: Children can follow routines, share and show kindness.
lessons.starter: Show the hand washing chart and say "We wash hands before snack."
teacherActivities: Remind children to wash before snack.
Watch each child wash and sing together.
Add a tick to the chart.
Say "Clean hands help us stay well."
learnerActivities: Children line up at the basin.
presentation: Step 1. Teacher: Remind children to wash before snack. Children: Children line up at the basin.
Step 2. Teacher: Watch each child wash and sing together. Children: Child washes with the song.
Step 3. Teacher: Add a tick to the chart. Children: Child ticks the chart.
Step 4. Teacher: Say "Clean hands help us stay well." Children: Children say clean hands.

practical.title: Wash before snack
practical.safety: Supervise closely and keep the floor dry. Use mild soap and clean towels.

differentiation.support: Wash together and name each step.
differentiation.extension: Ask the child to remind a friend.

assessment.method: Observe each child during the practical activity and note Emerging, Developing, Secure or Exceeding on the class record. Ask the questions below one to one or in a small group.

questions.question: When do we wash hands?
questions.expected: Before snack and after the toilet.

lessons.homeConnection: Make hand washing a family routine.
teacherReflection: Which children could show "wash hands without being reminded after a toilet visit or before eating" without help, and who needs another turn tomorrow?
What did the children say or do that I did not expect, and how will I use it in the next lesson?
Which resource or instruction worked best, and what would I change before I teach this again?

lessons.title: Week 8 hygiene check
lessons.subject: Social Habits
objectives: Teachers will observe how each child manages toilet routines and hand washing.
successCriteria: Tells an adult about toilet needs
lessons.previousKnowledge: Children can follow routines, share and show kindness.
lessons.starter: Sing the hand washing song and show three stations.
teacherActivities: Set up three stations: toilet words, steps and hand washing.
At each station watch what the child can do.
learnerActivities: Child answers with a word or action.
presentation: Step 1. Teacher: Set up three stations: toilet words, steps and hand washing. Children: Children rotate every four minutes.
Step 2. Teacher: At each station watch what the child can do. Children: Child answers with a word or action.
Step 3. Teacher: Record each child’s level. Children: Children tidy at the signal.

practical.title: Hygiene stations
practical.safety: Supervise each station and wipe spills at once. Use mild soap and clean towels and follow the school hygiene policy.

differentiation.support: Provide an adult partner and use one station.
differentiation.extension: Ask a confident child to explain hand washing to a friend.

assessment.method: Observe and record Emerging, Developing, Secure or Exceeding for: tells an adult about toilet needs; names toilet steps; washes hands with soap; dries hands.

expectedOutcomes: Has an observation record for Week 8
lessons.conclusion: Show clean hands and wave goodbye.
lessons.homeConnection: Share toilet progress with the teacher and keep routines the same.
teacherReflection: Which children could show "Teachers will observe how each child manages toilet routines and hand washing" without help, and who needs another turn tomorrow?
What did the children say or do that I did not expect, and how will I use it in the next lesson?
